one_liner: Rust hex codec with runtime-dispatched SIMD and const-fn API; near drop-in for `hex`, 6–100x faster on README benches.
what_it_does: Converts byte slices to and from ASCII hex. It copies the `hex` crate's surface (encode/encode_upper to String, decode to Vec<u8>, encode_to_slice/decode_to_slice, FromHex/ToHex traits, a FromHexError with the same three variants) so most code migrates by changing the import. It adds compile-time const fns (const_encode, const_decode_to_array, const_check), an itoa-style stack Buffer<N, PREFIX>, '0x'-prefixed encoders, display(), check() and serde helpers. It is no_std with optional alloc/std.
how_it_is_fast: Encoding splits each byte into nibbles and maps them through a 16-entry table with one byte-shuffle (pshufb/_mm256_shuffle_epi8 on x86, vqtbl1q_u8 on NEON), then interleaves with unpack/zip. With AVX2 that turns 32 input bytes into 64 characters per step. Since 2026-03, x86 decoding validates and decodes in one pass using Muła & Langdale's 'validating hex parse' Algorithm #3: saturating adds map digits and letters to 0..15, anything invalid lands above 15 and trips the sign bit, and vpmaddubsw merges nibble pairs (hi*16+lo) before a pack/permute. Output goes straight into uninitialized capacity. The CPU path (AVX2, then SSSE3/SSE2, then a scalar lookup table) is picked at runtime via is_x86_feature_detected! or cpufeatures.
when_to_use: Replacing `hex` on hot Rust paths that print or parse digests, keys or IDs; the README shows about 59x at 1 MB and still 6–14x at 32 bytes.
0x-prefixed hex strings: prefixed encoders exist and decode strips the prefix for you.
Hex constants built at compile time (const_decode_to_array, const_encode) or allocation-free formatting of fixed-size arrays through Buffer<N>.
Code shipping to aarch64 (NEON) or wasm32 with simd128, where the README positions it ahead of faster-hex, which only optimizes x86.
no_std or embedded crates that still want a SIMD fast path; only cfg-if and cpufeatures are required.
when_not_to_use: When you must match `hex`'s serde wire format exactly: `#[serde(with = "const_hex")]` writes a 0x prefix (see gotchas).
Strict parsers that must reject a leading '0x'/'0X': decode, decode_to_slice and check strip it silently.
The last few percent of x86 slice-encode throughput: in the README's encode_to_slice rows faster-hex was 6–12% faster from 2 kB up. There is no AVX-512 path.
Code that needs every safe API to be sound: issue #47 shows safe Buffer methods producing an invalid-UTF-8 &mut str (UB under Miri), closed by the maintainer as 'too contrived' to fix.
Non-Rust projects: the siblings cover C++ and Node.

integration.dependencies: cfg-if; cpufeatures on x86/x86-64; optional serde_core (feature `serde`) and proptest (internal fuzzing)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.64 (CI builds on 1.64, stable and nightly). The `core-error` feature needs Rust 1.81; the `nightly` and `portable-simd` features need nightly.
integration.platforms: Any target. SIMD paths: x86/x86-64 (SSE2/SSSE3/AVX2, detected at runtime), aarch64 NEON, wasm32 with simd128, and std::simd on nightly; a scalar lookup table elsewhere.
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the functions keep no state apart from cached CPU-feature detection, and Buffer is a plain owned value
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same function names, trait names and error variants as `hex`, but FromHexError is a separate type, decode also accepts a 0x/0X prefix, serde output adds a 0x prefix by default, and ToHex is deprecated

gotchas: Serde: `#[serde(with = "const_hex")]` serializes with a leading "0x", unlike `hex` (issue #34). Use `const_hex::serde::no_prefix` (1.18.0+) to keep the old JSON. Deserialization accepts both forms.
Decode is more permissive than `hex`: a leading 0x/0X is stripped before validation, so '0x…' strings that `hex` treats as invalid now parse.

`ToHex` is deprecated (open issue #26). The maintainer says its iterator-of-char API forces slow one-item-at-a-time output and keeps it only for `hex` compatibility, so migrations surface deprecation warnings; use ToHexExt, encode_to_slice or display().
Buffer::as_mut_byte_array() followed by as_mut_str() lets safe code build a non-UTF-8 str (issue #47). The maintainer won't fix it, so don't write non-ASCII bytes through the byte-array view.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: For Rust, pick const-hex over fast-hex (zbjornson, C++/Node) and hx (a NEON table-lookup encode experiment). Its older AVX2 unchecked-decode path descends from fast-hex via faster-hex, and it is the only one of the three shipped as a maintained crate with runtime dispatch, validation and a `hex`-compatible API.
verified_claims_summary: The README's libtest run used rustc 1.83.0-nightly (2024-10-03) on x86_64 Linux on an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X with the default bench profile. At 1 MB it shows decode 108,937 ns vs `hex` 6,409,294 ns (~59x), encode 30,716 ns vs 3,048,496 ns (~99x), and Display formatting ~158x faster than std. At 32 bytes the gap narrows to ~6x decode, ~7–8x slice encode and ~14x String encode (all derived from page data). The numbers predate the 2025–26 rewrites (divan/CodSpeed benches, single-pass AVX2 decode, NEON decode) and were not re-run.
status_note: Actively maintained: 1.19.3 released 2026-09-16, MSRV 1.64 tested in CI along with Miri and fuzzing, dual MIT/Apache-2.0, ~60.5M downloads and 166 reverse dependencies. The `hex` baseline's last release was 0.4.3 in 2021-03.
